text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant. with perspicacious discernment

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Malrotation with Midgut Volvulus

The presence of bilious vomiting in a newborn is a surgical emergency until proven otherwise. Although your family history mentions pyloric stenosis, the timing of symptoms immediately after birth strongly suggests a congenital malformation of the intestines rather than hypertrophic pyloric stenosis, which typically presents a few weeks later. I need to visualize your anatomy immediately to confirm if there is a twisting of the bowel. REQUEST IMAGES: Upper GI Series with contrast.
